Healthy Raspberry Cookies with Chocolate Chips

ByCatalina Castravet October 12, 2026October 12, 2026
Recipe Print
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 10:45
Instaread

Healthy Raspberry Cookies are a delicious treat made with fresh sweet raspberries, chewy oatmeal, and melty chocolate chips. To make them more filling and wholesome, I also like to add protein powder. They serve as a delicious, satisfying snack, dessert, or even a quick breakfast on the go.

I know people are divided on sweet vs. salty breakfasts; I’ve always preferred sweet. It just puts me in such a good mood. When I am in a hurry and don’t have time to fix something, I grab a protein raspberry cookie with either my strawberry smoothie or my creamy, flavorful pineapple smoothie, and call it a great morning.

These nutritious cookies are naturally gluten-free, made with gluten-free oats and healthy nut butter, and contain no refined sugars. I also like that I don’t have to chill these first; mix, roll, bake for a few minutes, and they are ready to eat. Since they are so easy to make, I usually whip a batch in the morning or after dinner so I always have them on hand.

Why you will love this recipe 

  • Tasty and good for you: With no added sugar, these sweet, tangy cookies are full of fruit, antioxidant-rich chocolate, and nutty almond butter. The kids love the flavor, and I love that they’re eating protein-packed snacks.
  • So fast and easy: I can make these cookies in less than 30 minutes from start to finish. Prep takes about 15 minutes, and they bake in about 10-12 minutes. 
  • Satisfying: This recipe uses lots of oats for fiber and protein powder, which helps me feel full even if I indulge in a delicious dessert.
  • Nut butter: Using nut butter instead of regular butter cuts down on saturated fat while keeping the cookies soft and chewy. I also like the mild nutty flavor that almond butter adds to these cookies.

What you will need

  • Produce: Mashed bananas provide sweetness, moisture, and a natural binder. Fresh raspberries add vibrant natural flavor and moisture, with bursts of tartness and bright color. 
  • Dry ingredients: Rolled oats add chewy structure, plus soluble fiber, protein, iron, and vitamins. Protein powder boosts the nutrients and helps you stay full longer, turning a treat into a healthy snack. It also slows glucose absorption to prevent blood sugar spikes. Chocolate chips add rich chocolate flavor, a satisfying bite, and an indulgent burst of gooey sweetness. 
  • Wet ingredients: Almond butter replaces butter as a binder and moisturizer, keeping the cookies soft and tender with less fat.

How to prepare

Preheat the oven: Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a large cookie sheet with parchment paper. 

Mix the batter: While the oven heats, I combine all ingredients except the berries and chocolate chips in a large bowl. Then, I fold in the chocolate chips and raspberries with a rubber spatula. 

Scoop the cookies: Use a cookie scoop to form 12 dough balls and place them on the cookie sheet, pressing them down slightly. 

Bake the cookies: Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown. 

Let them cool: Remove them from the oven and let them cool completely on the cookie sheet. 

Serve or store: Finally, I remove them from the pan and serve them or store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator. 

Expert tip

Freeze the raspberries

Raspberries have a lot of moisture and tend to spread it around when you mix them into the batter. I don’t mix mine in until after everything else is combined, but even then, they can make quite a mess if they are extra fresh and juicy. One of the best tips I have ever gotten was to flash-freeze my fresh berries to firm them up before mixing them in. They don’t have to be frozen solid. Put them in the freezer for 20 to 30 minutes, until they’re almost solid, so they don’t bleed and the cookies aren’t too watery.

More tips to consider:

  • Measure the oats carefully using the spoon-and-level method or a kitchen scale to avoid dried-out cookies.
  • If the dough is too sticky, refrigerate it for 20 to 30 minutes before scooping. 
  • Use freeze-dried raspberries for a more intense flavor and don’t worry about runny fruit. 
  • If bananas aren’t ripe, put them in a bag with a ripe apple, pear, or avocado to speed up ripening. To speed it up even more, microwave them for 30 seconds.
  • It is better to underbake the cookies slightly than to overbake them. Remove them when they are still slightly soft, and they will finish setting on the hot cookie sheet.

Recipe variations and add-ins:

  • Other berries: If raspberries aren’t available, try these with strawberries, blueberries, or blackberries. They actually taste amazing with any fruit, including apple chunks, peaches, pears, or mandarin orange pieces. 
  • More crunch: I sometimes add nuts to make these crunchier. I like chopped peanuts or pecans, but walnuts, almonds, or hazelnuts work well too.  
  • Different chocolate: Instead of semisweet chocolate chips, try white or dark chocolate chips for a different flavor. 
  • Caramel sauce: To make these richer and more luscious, drizzle some of my homemade caramel sauce on top. 
  • Add zest: Add a bit of orange, lemon, or lime zest for a tangy twist.  

Serving suggestions:

These delicious cookies go great with a glass of ice-cold milk or a cup of hot coffee. I enjoy serving them warm for breakfast, topped with a big dollop of vanilla Greek yogurt and a spoonful of homemade strawberry jam. It tastes like a delicious dessert while still being packed with good-for-you stuff.

Another way to serve these is with a bowl of ice cream. I like vanilla, but try my easy Oreo ice cream recipe. It only has 3 ingredients and takes just a few minutes to prepare. It is also delicious with this strawberry sorbet. You only need fruit, honey, and a splash of lime juice to make this tangy treat. I also enjoy them with my fruit salad; the kids love this combo.

How to store leftovers:

  • Refrigerate: Leftover cookies will stay fresh at room temperature for up to a week in an airtight container or in the fridge for 2 weeks.
  • Freezing: I freeze leftovers in freezer bags for up to 6 months.    
  • Defrost: I thaw frozen leftover cookies in the fridge overnight before serving.  

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to use protein powder?

No, instead of protein powder, use oat flour for complex carbohydrates, fiber, and natural structure. Or grind a bit of the rolled oats into a powder. Another option is to add some almond flour or ground flax. These add healthy fats and omega-3 fatty acids. Greek yogurt or eggs can also add moisture and natural binding without relying on a powdered supplement. 

Can I use frozen raspberries instead of fresh?

Yes, frozen raspberries will work great. In fact, they will be perfect. Just don’t let them thaw, or they will bleed all over the batter. Add them while they are still frozen, so they don’t turn the cookies mushy. As my expert tip says, flash-frozen berries work better because fresh berries tend to lose too much juice and make the batter extra watery. 

How do I keep these cookies from spreading too much?

Since they use so little liquid, the cookies shouldn’t spread much. The protein and almond butter make a thick paste if you measure everything properly. If it doesn’t seem thick enough or solid, roll it into a ball and chill it for about 30 minutes before forming the cookies. This should prevent any spreading problems.

Can I use quick oats instead of rolled oats?

Yes, quick oats will work, but they will change the cookies’ texture. Because they are cut into smaller pieces and rolled thinner, they blend into the dough more easily, making the cookies softer and less chewy. They also absorb more moisture, so the cookies may turn out drier if you don’t adjust the recipe.

Healthy Raspberry Cookies with Chocolate Chips

Protein-Packed Healthy Raspberry Cookies are gluten-free and free of refined sugar, with fresh raspberries, oats, and chocolate chips.
5 from 6 votes
Print Pin Rate
Course: Breakfast, Cookies, Dessert, Snack
Cuisine: American
Diet: Gluten Free, Kosher, Vegetarian
Keyword: Healthy Raspberry Cookies
Prep Time: 15 minutes minutes
Cook Time: 12 minutes minutes
Total Time: 27 minutes minutes
Servings: 12 cookies
Calories: 148kcal
Author: Catalina Castravet

Ingredients

  • 2 cups rolled oats gluten-free
  • 2 tablespoons protein powder of your choice
  • 2 large bananas mashed
  • 1/2 cup no sugar added almond butter or any other nut butter
  • 1/3 cup raspberries fresh
  • 1/4 cup chocolate chips optional or you can use sugar-free
US Customary – Metric

Instructions

  • Preheat the oven to 180C/350F.
  • Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside. You may have to use two baking sheets or bake the cookies in batches.
  • In a large mixing bowl, combine all the ingredients except for the raspberries and chocolate chips. Use a rubber spatula to fold them in at the end.
  • Form 12 small balls of dough and arrange them on the prepared baking sheet/s, 6 cookies or 8 per baking sheet. Press each ball into a cookie shape.
  • Bake for 12 minutes, or until the edges are golden.
  • Remove from the oven and let them cool completely on the tray before serving.

Notes

Freeze the raspberries

Raspberries have a lot of moisture and tend to spread it around when you mix them into the batter. I don’t mix mine in until after everything else is combined, but even then, they can make quite a mess if they are extra fresh and juicy. One of the best tips I have ever gotten was to flash-freeze my fresh berries to firm them up before mixing them in. They don’t have to be frozen solid. Put them in the freezer for 20 to 30 minutes, until they’re almost solid, so they don’t bleed and the cookies aren’t too watery.

More tips to consider:

  • Measure the oats carefully using the spoon-and-level method or a kitchen scale to avoid dried-out cookies.
  • If the dough is too sticky, refrigerate it for 20 to 30 minutes before scooping. 
  • Use freeze-dried raspberries for a more intense flavor and don’t worry about runny fruit. 
  • If bananas aren’t ripe, put them in a bag with a ripe apple, pear, or avocado to speed up ripening. To speed it up even more, microwave them for 30 seconds.
  • It is better to underbake the cookies slightly than to overbake them. Remove them when they are still slightly soft, and they will finish setting on the hot cookie sheet.
